On Mon, Aug 1, 2016 at 3:50 AM, <avian....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all,
I tried to calculate fit indices in three different groups (9 polytoumnous items, 246 examinees; 3  polytoumnous items 2266 examinees and 3 polytoumnous items 240 examinees); missing values were imputed.

M2 (or rather M2*) has the unfortunate property that it cannot be computed if the number of items is too small. Here, 3 items probably doesn't give enough degrees of freedom relative to the number of estimated parameters. I'm debating adding a fix for this sometime, where the marginals aren't completely collapsed, but it's not high on my todo list. 

That being said, what can you really conclude about the fit of a 3 item test? That model is *just* identified, so you're really asking for a lot of extra information while providing little room to move. 

Phil
